context.objective: Document how we carry out Client Data Migration, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: It kicks off when a new client is onboarded, when a fund changes administrators, or when historical data has to be migrated into Entrilia or Allvue. There is no fixed schedule, it is as needed. First the Manager and I as the preparer confirm the migration scope and target: the entities, the historical period, the target system, the types of data, the source provider and the output reports we will need. We also confirm it is a client onboarding migration and not the separate Allvue to Entrilia platform program, and we identify the approvals and milestones. The Manager has to confirm the scope before any mapping starts.
Once the Manager confirms the scope, how do you map the source data to the target?

Mapping does not come straight after scope, and honestly the mapping itself is not something I can describe well. What I do next, as the preparer, is receive and inventory the source package from the client or prior administrator: the detailed general ledger from the fund's start, the trial balance, prior reports, investor reference data, contact and banking data, the client chart of accounts, plus the target chart of accounts and transcodes and the upload templates. I list each file with its entity, period, version and provider in the intake log, keep an unchanged copy of every source file, and record anything missing or replaced. I check the package against the approved scope. How the mapping is done after that I am not sure about.
What happens when the source package is missing something or does not match the approved scope?

That is my third step, validating the source for completeness and internal consistency. I confirm the general ledger covers the period from the fund's start through the migration cutoff date. I compare the general ledger and trial balance periods and totals and identify differences. I check for missing or duplicate rows and files and for incomplete required fields. I check the investor reference, contact and banking data against the agreed scope. If there are problems I ask the source provider to clarify or correct them. I do this in the intake checks and the reconciliation workbook, and the Manager reviews significant issues. If the source is incomplete I stop: we do not treat it as ready for migration unless the Manager approves that decision, and we never fill gaps without recording them. If it is complete it moves on to mapping.
What tells you the migration is finished?

I do not know exactly what the Manager looks at, that is on their side. What I know is that I bring them the validated files, the issues that were resolved and the list of remaining issues, and they decide whether incomplete source data can go forward. There is no defined threshold for what counts as significant that I am aware of, and I do not know of any tolerance or a written rule on who else may accept incomplete data.
What is the practical impact when a migration is delayed because the source data is incomplete?

I only know that part second hand because the end is handled by other people. As I understand it, once the Manager gives final sign-off the account is handed off to the first accounting close, which is a separate process. The migration only counts as complete when the source and target reports fully agree with no unexplained difference and the Manager's sign-off is kept. Beyond that I am not sure what it enables.
What can go wrong if migrated data does not agree with the source, and what is the practical consequence?

What we need before starting is a client onboarding or administrator transition request and a decision on the target system. I do not know of a standard scope form or a set channel that the request arrives through, and there is no standard timeline or milestone calendar. After my validation step the rest, building the workbook mapping, the uploads, the import, the reports and the reconciliation, I cannot walk you through reliably. I know the import itself is done by someone else but I am not sure exactly who.
What does the completed migration enable for the client or the team?

memo_findings.answer: The work migrates historical client data into a target system, which may be Entrilia or Allvue.

The work is initiated when a new client is onboarded, when a fund changes administrators, or when historical data has to be migrated into Entrilia or Allvue. It is done as needed, with no fixed schedule.
Before starting, a client onboarding or administrator transition request and a target-system decision are needed. The participant reports no standard timeline or milestone calendar.
The participant does not know of a set channel for the request; who receives or detects it is not established.
The participant understands secondhand that migration is complete only when source and target reports fully agree with no unexplained difference and the Manager's sign-off is retained.

The Manager confirms the migration scope before mapping starts; the speaker is the preparer.
The role accountable for the overall migration result, distinct from the Manager's scope confirmation and the speaker's preparer role, is not established.

Before mapping starts, the Manager and the speaker, who is the preparer, confirm the migration scope and target: entities, historical period, target system, data types, source provider, and needed output reports. They also confirm whether it is a client-onboarding migration rather than the separate Allvue-to-Entrilia platform program, and identify approvals and milestones.
After scope confirmation, the preparer receives and inventories the source package from the client or prior administrator, before mapping.
The preparer lists each file's entity, period, version and provider in the intake log, keeps an unchanged copy of every source file, records missing or replaced items, and checks the package against approved scope.
The preparer is unsure how mapping is performed after intake.
Third, the preparer validates source completeness and internal consistency: checks that the general ledger covers fund inception through the migration cutoff, compares ledger and trial balance periods and totals, identifies differences, checks for missing or duplicate rows and files and incomplete required fields, and checks investor reference, contact and banking data against agreed scope.
For problems the preparer asks the source provider to clarify or correct them. Complete source moves to mapping; incomplete source is stopped unless the Manager approves it going forward, and gaps are recorded.
According to the participant's secondhand understanding, after the Manager's final sign-off the account is handed off to the separate first accounting close process.
After validation, the participant identifies workbook mapping, uploads, import, reports and reconciliation as later work, but cannot reliably walk through it. Someone other than the participant performs the import; the exact person is unknown.

The Manager must confirm the scope before any mapping starts.
Scope confirmation criteria and evidence, scope rejection or rework handling, and any approvals beyond the reported Manager decisions and final sign-off remain unspecified.
The preparer checks the source package against approved scope and records anything missing or replaced in the intake log.
The preparer performs source completeness and consistency checks in the intake checks and reconciliation workbook; the Manager reviews significant issues. The preparer brings the Manager validated files, resolved issues and a list of remaining issues for the incomplete-source decision.
The preparer does not know exactly what the Manager examines when deciding whether incomplete source data may proceed, and is not aware of a defined significance threshold.
The participant reports secondhand that final completion requires full agreement of source and target reports without unexplained differences and retained Manager sign-off.
